title: Every power torsion module admits a resolution by direct sums of quotients of the ring by powers of the ideal
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement says that every I-power torsion module M admits a resolution by direct sums of copies of R over I^n for varying n (statement lines 24001-24011). The proof is a compact but complete construction: it exhibits the canonical surjection from the direct sum over the elements m of M of the modules R over I^{n_m}, where n_m is the smallest exponent killing m, observes that the source is power torsion and that its kernel is a submodule of a power torsion module and therefore again power torsion, and iterates the same step on the successive kernels (proof lines 24014-24020). The two points that make the induction work are the choice of the exponent attached to each element and the inheritance of power torsionness by submodules, and both are stated explicitly. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.
